clue.text: Employees in one section of "the week" magazine?

indicators.note: in is the insertion signal, and a loose one: it stands ahead of both pieces, where a stricter clue would put it between the weekday phrase and the magazine

parts.note: Ms is an American feminist magazine, founded in 1971
an, the indefinite article, means one
Friday is one of the seven days that make up the week; the quotation marks do no work beyond making the phrase look like a title, and the question mark allows for the example

explanation.surface: The staff who work in one department of The Week, a news magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a pure cryptic definition, but every word works: 'in' signals insertion, 'the week' is just seven days, and the magazine is a feminist title from America, not The Week, the British news digest.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Robinson Crusoe's servant, these are devoted assistants or general helpers, especially in an office, so they are hired staff.

clue.text: Firmly closed broadcast having had excess booze

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
tight is informal for drunk

explanation.surface: A radio show was shut down for good after someone drank far too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a container sealed so that nothing can get in or out is shut as firmly as can be.

clue.text: Banking authority supplied with power?

definitions.meaning: the everyday short name for the Federal Reserve, the central bank of the United States
a machine or circuit given its fuel or current is said to be this, the past tense of feed

explanation.surface: A financial regulator is handed the authority it needs.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that power is only one thing a machine or circuit can be supplied with; the surface makes 'power' sound like legal authority.
explanation.definitionFit: The short name of America's central bank is also the past tense of feed, used of a machine given its current or fuel.

clue.text: Hopeless writer's shown up in appeal

indicators.note: in places the upturned writing tool inside the short word for appeal

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal, as in 'she's got it'

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means the word is written from the bottom to the top

parts.note: a pen is a thing that writes, so a writer; the 's is only a joining 'is'

explanation.surface: A useless author is embarrassed during a court appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown up' is a down-clue reversal, turning the writing tool into NEP, and 'in' is the insertion signal; 'appeal' is the sex appeal of old slang, not a court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone clumsy and incompetent at a task is no good at it at all.

clue.text: Southern Turkish city containing no aitch? Wrong!

indicators.note: wrong says the letters before it are not in their right order and must be put another way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims a city's name has no letter H in it and is told that is incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong!' is the anagram signal for NO AITCH. The surface is also true of the city: its name does have an H in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the ancient city, now called Antakya, lies in Hatay province in the far south of Turkey.

clue.text: Replacement appears reconditioned? Right

indicators.note: something reconditioned has been stripped down and rebuilt, so the word before it is rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Rt is a standard abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon for Right Honourable

explanation.surface: A substitute component looks as if it has been refurbished, and someone agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconditioned' rearranges APPEARS into SPAREPA, and RT, as in Rt Hon, finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a component kept in reserve to take the place of one that breaks or wears out.

clue.text: Extra score

definitions.meaning: British slang, originally naval, for spare or surplus to requirements
to score a surface is to cut a long deep line into it

explanation.surface: A bonus run or point added to the tally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' is a cut here, not a tally, and 'Extra' is the Royal Navy slang sense of spare or surplus.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the word means spare or surplus, and it is also a long deep cut such as scoring makes.

clue.text: End with mean scoring ratio

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose, as in 'to that end', and so is a goal
the mean of a set of numbers is their average

explanation.surface: A team finishes the season with a miserly rate of points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' only joins the two halves. 'mean' reads as stingy but is the arithmetical kind; English league football used this ratio until goal difference replaced it in 1976.
explanation.definitionFit: In football it is goals scored divided by goals conceded, once used to separate British league teams level on points.

clue.text: No lager's served up in such clothing

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the two words are delivered from the bottom to the top

parts.note: taken as written
Pils, short for Pilsner, is a pale lager; the 's is only a joining 'is'

explanation.surface: A pub refuses to pour beer for anyone dressed like that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns NO PILS upside down in this down clue. 'Such' leans on the answer itself: clothing of the kind those upturned letters name.
explanation.definitionFit: Example by description: a shoe or garment with no laces or fastenings, simply pulled over the foot or body, is clothing of this kind.

clue.text: Slope: garden with it is dodgy

indicators.note: something dodgy is unsound and liable to give way, so the letters of the two words before it shift about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A garden on a hillside, and whatever comes with it, proves unsafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is dodgy' is the anagram signal, covering GARDEN and IT together; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the steepness of a hill, road or line on a graph is its incline.

clue.text: One soldier in a party going slowly in work

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first in places the phrase for one soldier inside the phrase for a party

parts.note: a do is an informal British word for a party or celebration
one can be written as the indefinite article a
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A lone squaddie at a party is dragging their feet on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first 'in' is the insertion signal. The second belongs to the definition, where 'work' means music and the answer is its Italian tempo marking.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction from Italian: a passage so marked in a composition is played at a leisurely tempo.

clue.text: Pressure one found in diplomacy recalled another game

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the whole assembly is read from right to left
found in places the pressure-and-one pair inside the word for diplomacy

parts.note: tact is skill in dealing with people without giving offence
P is the physics symbol for pressure
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The strain someone felt during international negotiations brought a different pastime to mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts PI inside TACT to give TACPIT, and 'recalled' turns that round. 'Another' is fair because Diplomacy is itself a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: An old street pastime in which a short tapered stick is flicked into the air and hit with a longer one.

clue.text: A firm tummy

definitions.meaning: a business company, a body legally allowed to act as a single person
in jocular British use the word means a large belly or paunch

explanation.surface: A stomach with good muscle tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' is a noun here, a company, not an adjective describing the tummy; the paunch sense is a jocular British one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a business company, and in jocular British use also a prominent paunch.

clue.text: Poor rate for working agent

indicators.note: for working says the two words before it are material to be worked, as clay is worked into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Miserable pay for a spy on active duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder: 'for working' is the signal, covering both POOR and RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-synonym: each names a person who acts or carries out business for others, as a travel firm does for holidaymakers.

clue.text: There's food in the end by way of going round ring road

indicators.note: in the end says the food comes last, though the clue mentions it first
going round means the word for by way of wraps itself about the ring

parts.note: through means by way of, as in 'we drove through France'
the letter O is shaped like a ring
fare is food and drink as provided, as in 'pub fare'

explanation.surface: Drive round the orbital route and you will eventually come to something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring road' must be split: 'going round' is the container signal and 'ring' what it contains, 'in the end' sends the food to the back, and 'road' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a public street or highway open at both ends, along which traffic passes.

clue.text: Trip to lunch with journalist — not like this!

definitions.note: the whole clue is the hint: this is the state in which nobody would go out to eat with a reporter

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the letters of the next two words tumble into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: Someone heading out for a meal with a reporter is told not to go looking like that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' is the anagram signal for TO LUNCH. The definition leans on the whole clue: the state in which nobody would set off to meet a reporter over a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusive rather than a synonym: bare, with nothing on, is how nobody would set off for a meal with a reporter.

clue.text: Lethargic, lacking what's essential for shopping

definitions.meaning: drained of energy and enthusiasm, too sluggish to stir
a pun, not a dictionary sense: split in two, the word says 'without' the written reminder of what to buy

explanation.surface: Someone sluggish hasn't got the money or energy needed for a trip round the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun, not a dictionary sense: split the answer after its fourth letter and it says the shopper is without that written reminder.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means drained of energy, and split in two it whimsically describes a shopper with nothing written down to buy.

clue.text: Rpo is involved with theatrics from here?

definitions.note: this place: the clue as a whole says where such players and a stage show meet

indicators.note: involved can mean tangled or complicated, so the letters of the words on either side are tangled up together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: London's Royal Philharmonic gets caught up in some stage drama coming from this very spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is involved with' is the anagram signal for the words either side. RPO is London's Royal Philharmonic, so the whole clue also describes the place: where players sit to accompany a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: The sunken area in front of a stage is where musicians sit to accompany an opera, ballet or musical.

clue.text: Printing mistake is dumb, keeping a bishop up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole assembly is read from the bottom to the top
keeping means the word for dumb holds the a-and-bishop pair inside it

parts.note: mute means unable to speak, the older sense of dumb
taken as written
RR stands for Right Reverend, the title given to a bishop

explanation.surface: A silly typo is stopping a clergyman from getting to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' is the container signal, and 'up' turns the whole of MUTARRE upside down in this down clue; bishops are styled Right Reverend, hence the pair of Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an error in a published text, of the kind listed on a correction slip.

clue.text: Get away with individual request being first

indicators.note: being first says the word for request leads, though the clue names the individual before it

parts.note: to beg is to ask earnestly for something
an individual is a single person, a one

explanation.surface: Someone escapes blame because a personal plea was dealt with before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get away with' reads as escaping blame, but 'Get away' alone is the definition, an order to leave; 'being first' moves BEG ahead of ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are commands telling someone to leave at once, the answer being the old-fashioned form.

clue.text: Book on English party: discuss at length

indicators.note: on only joins here: the pieces run in clue order, not the swapped order that stricter across clues give this word

parts.note: Labour is one of the main British political parties

explanation.surface: A volume about a political party in England goes over it in great detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to dwell on a point and argue it in excessive detail, going on about it far too long.

clue.text: Iron shirt with no tails quickly

indicators.note: a word's tail is its last letter, and the plural says each of the two words loses its own

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them
a top is any garment for the upper body, such as a shirt

explanation.surface: Press a dress shirt, the kind without tails, in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no tails' works on both words: PRESS and TOP each lose their last letter, leaving PRES and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction from Italian meaning at a fast tempo, and a conjuror's word for at once.

clue.text: Heard acclaim for quarries

indicators.note: heard says the word for acclaim is to be listened to, and a word that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: praise is warm public approval, which is acclaim

explanation.surface: Word got round of public approval for the stone pits.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a quarry is a hunted animal or victim, so several of them are these.

clue.text: Second plate is fashionable

parts.note: a mo is informal British for a moment, as in 'half a mo', and a second is a moment too
a dish is a plate or shallow bowl for serving food

explanation.surface: Going back for another plateful is all the rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in the current style, following the latest trend.

clue.text: Generate conflict? One may do

definitions.note: one here is a person, and 'may do' points back to the first two words: someone who may cause strife

indicators.note: conflict sets the letters of the word before it at odds with one another, breaking up their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Does someone stir up trouble? A certain sort of person might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conflict' is the anagram signal for GENERATE. The definition leans back on those words: someone who may well stir up strife at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusive: an adolescent is proverbially someone likely to stir up rows with parents.

clue.text: Scottish resort? Yes, right

parts.note: ay, also spelt aye, is a Scots and northern English word for yes

explanation.surface: Asked whether a place is a Scottish holiday town, someone confirms it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside town on the Firth of Clyde in south-west Scotland, long popular for its beach and racecourse.

clue.text: Hold back in shower as reported

indicators.note: as reported means the word for shower is taken as spoken, and a word that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: a shower is a short fall of rain

explanation.surface: Someone is said to linger in the bathroom while washing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to check or restrain, as a rider slows a horse by pulling on the straps.

clue.text: Block request mounted for hardy flower

parts.note: to dam a stream is to block its flow
to ask for something is to request it
rose means went up, as mounted does in 'the tension mounted'

explanation.surface: Stop the order that someone has put together for a tough garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: An old, strongly scented pink bloom grown for perfume oil, on a shrub tough enough to stand cold winters.
